name: devup-vscode
description: Sidebar tree, status bar, and live logs for @gachlab/devup — control your dev stack without leaving the editor.

devup.projectName.description: Override the devup project name (normally auto-detected from devup.config.*). Used to resolve the control-plane socket at ~/.devup/sock-<name>.sock, and the log folder at ~/.devup/logs/<name>/ — the latter even when devup.socketPath is set, which otherwise ignores this.

devup.socketPath.description: Override the control-plane socket path entirely. When set, devup.projectName is ignored.

devup.executablePath.description: Path to devup executable. If empty, uses 'npx devup' which searches node_modules first, then global PATH.

enumDescriptions: Forward every service port — default. A web app is useless without the APIs it calls.
Forward web service ports only. The frontends load, but their API calls will not resolve.
Stop forwarding new ports. Tunnels already open stay open; close them from the Ports view.
devup.portForwarding.description: In a remote window (Remote-SSH, Dev Containers, WSL, Codespaces), ask the editor to tunnel devup service ports back to you. The daemon spawns services detached, so VS Code cannot auto-detect them. The Ports view shows the address to use: usually http://localhost:<port>, though the editor remaps the port when it is already taken locally, and Codespaces publishes to a hosted URL instead. Individual ports can be excluded with remote.portsAttributes onAutoForward "ignore". Ignored in local windows.

enumDescriptions: Group by service type (APIs / Webs) — default
devup.treeView.groupBy.description: How to group services in the sidebar tree.

devup.profile.description: Active profile filter. When set, only services belonging to this profile are shown. Leave empty to show all services.

devup.stats.cpuWarnThreshold.description: CPU% threshold for warning icon on service tree items.

devup.stats.memWarnThresholdMB.description: Memory (MB) threshold for warning icon on service tree items.

devup.stats.cpuHighThreshold.description: CPU% threshold for red (critical) icon on service tree items.

devup.stats.memHighThresholdMB.description: Memory (MB) threshold for red (critical) icon on service tree items.

devup.debug.browser.description: Browser to launch for 'Debug the stack'. In a remote window the editor launches it on your local machine and tunnels the debug port back.

devup.logDir.description: Root of devup's log directory, when the daemon was started with --log-dir. Empty = ~/.devup/logs. The daemon does not publish this over the control plane, so it has to be repeated here for 'Open log file' to find anything.

devup.notifications.configReload.description: Show a notification when the daemon hot-reloads the config and services are added or removed.

walkthroughs.title: Debug your devup stack
walkthroughs.description: Attach a debugger to a service without taking it out of devup — and follow a request from the frontend into the API.

steps.title: Start the stack
steps.description:
The extension talks to a running daemon over its control-plane socket. A service you cannot see is a service you cannot attach to.
[Start daemon](command:devup.daemon.start)

steps.title: Attach to one service
steps.description:
Right-click a service in the devup sidebar, or run the command. It restarts under the Node inspector and the editor attaches.
[Debug a service](command:devup.debugService)

steps.title: Or just press F5
steps.description:
One entry per service in the Run and Debug picker, with no launch.json — and no port written down, because it changes on every restart.
[Open Run and Debug](command:workbench.view.debug)

steps.title: Follow a request front to back
steps.description:
Opens the frontend in a debugged browser and attaches to the services you pick, with their breakpoints bound before the page loads.
[Debug the stack](command:devup.debugStack)

steps.title: Turn it off when you are done
steps.description:
The --inspect flag lives on the service in the daemon, not in your editor session — so it outlives both the crash you were chasing and the window you were in.
[Stop debugging](command:devup.stopDebugging)

service.description: The devup service to attach to. Omit to be asked. The service is restarted under the Node inspector if it is not already.

No devup daemon is running for this project.
[Start daemon (devup up -d)](command:devup.daemon.start)
[Why can't it be reached?](command:devup.diagnostics)

The socket for this project exists, but the daemon is not answering — it may still be starting, may be wedged, or the file may be left over from a crash.
[Restart daemon](command:devup.daemon.restart)
[Show connection details](command:devup.diagnostics)

The project name could not be read from your devup config, so the socket path was guessed from the folder name — which matches a running daemon only by coincidence.
[Set the project name](command:devup.setProjectName)
[Show connection details](command:devup.diagnostics)

Open the folder that holds your devup.config.* to control its stack from here.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

[Open devup documentation](https://github.com/gachlab/devup#readme)

[Set the project name](command:devup.setProjectName)
